arks.name: testing-strategy
arks.description: For tech leads and QA owners: plan what to test at which level, rank risks, read coverage honestly and write a test strategy doc agents can follow.

arks.name: tdd
arks.description: For developers practising TDD: red-green-refactor discipline, test lists, step sizing and outside-in design so agents write tests before code.

arks.name: property-based-testing
arks.description: For developers adding property-based tests: finding good properties, writing generators that shrink well, stateful model tests and pinning failures.

arks.name: playwright-e2e
arks.description: For teams testing web apps with Playwright: resilient locators, auth fixtures, visual checks, trace debugging and sharded CI runs.

arks.name: cypress-e2e
arks.description: For teams on Cypress: retry-safe tests, custom commands, network stubbing, component tests and parallel CI.

arks.name: integration-testing
arks.description: For backend developers: integration tests with real databases and brokers via Testcontainers, isolated test data, contract tests and stubbed third parties.

arks.name: unit-testing
arks.description: For any developer writing unit tests: clear structure, the right test double, readable names, parameterised cases and spotting test smells.

arks.name: mutation-testing
arks.description: For teams who want tests that really check behaviour: incremental mutation testing setup, survivor triage and coverage reports read critically.

arks.name: flaky-tests
arks.description: For teams fighting unreliable CI: detecting and classifying flaky tests, quarantining them with owners and fixing nondeterminism at the source.

arks.name: load-testing
arks.description: For engineers validating capacity: planning load, stress and soak tests, writing k6 scripts, analysing results and benchmarking fairly.

arks.name: test-suite-speed
arks.description: For teams whose tests are too slow: profiling the suite, safe parallelism, test impact analysis and timing-based CI sharding.

arks.name: qa-test-design
arks.description: For QA engineers and developers: deriving test cases with classic techniques, exploratory charters, criteria-to-test mapping and solid bug reports.

arks.name: bdd-gherkin
arks.description: For teams using BDD: example mapping, declarative Gherkin scenarios, maintainable step definitions and living documentation.

arks.name: snapshot-testing
arks.description: For developers testing complex outputs: snapshot hygiene, golden files and approval-test workflows that catch real changes without rubber-stamping updates.

arks.name: test-data
arks.description: For developers tired of brittle fixtures: test data builders, factories with traits, shared dataset management and synthetic data instead of production copies.

arks.name: code-review
arks.description: For reviewers and teams: multi-pass review checklists, risk-based review depth, kind actionable comments, a written review policy and sensible CODEOWNERS.

arks.name: pull-requests
arks.description: For developers opening PRs: self-review, clear descriptions, small split changes, stacked PRs and good commit messages.

arks.name: refactoring
arks.description: For developers improving existing code: recognising smells, applying named refactorings in safe steps and changing interfaces with parallel change.

arks.name: legacy-code
arks.description: For developers changing untested legacy code: mapping the system, finding seams, pinning behaviour with characterization tests and removing dead code.

arks.name: legacy-modernisation
arks.description: For architects replacing legacy systems: assessing options, strangler-fig and branch-by-abstraction migrations, monolith decomposition and parity verification.

arks.name: large-scale-changes
arks.description: For platform and infra teams making repo-wide changes: codemods, structural search-and-replace, renames at scale and owner-sharded rollouts.

arks.name: tech-debt
arks.description: For tech leads managing debt: a debt register, churn-times-complexity hotspots, interest-based prioritisation and paydown proposals leadership will fund.

arks.name: domain-driven-design
arks.description: For teams modelling complex domains: bounded contexts, aggregates, ubiquitous language, context maps and event storming.

arks.name: architecture-decisions
arks.description: For teams recording architecture decisions: ADR writing and lifecycle, trade-off matrices and a short set of architecture principles.

arks.name: design-docs
arks.description: For engineers proposing significant changes: design doc structure, a lightweight RFC process, rigorous doc review and option comparison.

arks.name: system-design
arks.description: For engineers designing scalable systems: a design framework, capacity estimates, scaling and caching patterns and consistency choices.

arks.name: event-driven-architecture
arks.description: For teams building on events and messages: event design, schema versioning, outbox, idempotent consumers, sagas and CQRS/event sourcing.

arks.name: modular-architecture
arks.description: For teams keeping a codebase modular: hexagonal architecture, modular monoliths, enforced dependency rules, fitness functions and coupling metrics.

arks.name: microservices-design
arks.description: For teams splitting or running services: boundary design, communication styles, distributed failure modes and resilience patterns.

arks.name: architecture-docs
arks.description: For architects and leads documenting systems: C4 diagrams, diagrams as code, arc42 and a readable one-page architecture overview.

arks.name: git-workflows
arks.description: For teams agreeing how they use git: branching models, trunk-based development, Conventional Commits, rebasing and commit messages.

arks.name: git-power-tools
arks.description: For developers who want git to stop being scary: bisect, reflog recovery, conflict resolution, history rewriting, worktrees and large files.

arks.name: monorepo
arks.description: For teams running monorepos: layout and dependency rules, affected-only builds, versioning, repo consolidation and Nx/Turborepo or Bazel setup.

arks.name: technical-writing
arks.description: For engineers who write docs: clear style, Diátaxis organisation, information architecture, editing passes and plain-language rewrites.

arks.name: project-docs
arks.description: For maintainers of any repo: READMEs, contributing guides, quickstarts, troubleshooting guides and useful code comments.

arks.name: api-documentation
arks.description: For teams documenting APIs and SDKs: complete reference docs, tested examples, task guides, SDK docs and API changelogs.

arks.name: docs-as-code
arks.description: For teams keeping docs in the repo: PR-reviewed docs pipelines, static docs sites, prose linting, link checking and versioned docs.

arks.name: debugging
arks.description: For developers chasing bugs: hypothesis-driven debugging, minimal repros, targeted logging, debugger techniques and git bisect.

arks.name: hard-bug-hunting
arks.description: For senior engineers on the nastiest bugs: race conditions, intermittent failures, production-only issues and crash dumps.

arks.name: performance-profiling
arks.description: For engineers making code faster: CPU flame graphs, memory leak hunting, latency analysis, benchmarks, regression detection and an optimisation playbook.

arks.name: dependency-upgrades
arks.description: For teams keeping dependencies current: upgrade planning, breaking-change triage, lockfile hygiene, update-bot config and major framework upgrades.

arks.name: oss-maintenance
arks.description: For open source maintainers: issue triage, contributor onboarding, governance docs and protecting maintainer time.

arks.name: oss-project-setup
arks.description: For anyone publishing a new open source project: license choice, community files, issue and PR templates, README and versioning policy.

arks.name: release-management
arks.description: For release owners: checklist-driven releases, release branches and backports, hotfixes and fixed-cadence release trains.

arks.name: changelogs-versioning
arks.description: For library and product teams: semver policy, human changelogs, automated versioning, release notes and deprecation policy.

arks.name: codebase-onboarding
arks.description: For engineers joining a codebase and the people onboarding them: codebase tours, architecture discovery, onboarding guides and domain glossaries.

arks.name: code-archaeology
arks.description: For developers who need to understand why code exists before changing it: git history digging, call-graph and data-flow tracing and ownership mapping.

arks.name: engineering-one-on-ones
arks.description: For engineering managers: 1:1 preparation, SBI feedback, career conversations against a ladder and effective delegation.

arks.name: estimation-planning
arks.description: For teams planning delivery: range estimates, vertical story splitting, sprint planning and Monte Carlo forecasts instead of guesses.

arks.name: engineering-metrics
arks.description: For engineering leaders measuring delivery: DORA metrics, PR cycle time, flow metrics and developer experience surveys, read without gaming.

arks.name: engineering-planning
arks.description: For engineering leads: quarterly planning with capacity splits, technical roadmaps, project kickoff docs and crisp status updates.

arks.name: team-rituals
arks.description: For engineering managers and team leads: retrospectives that lead to change, useful standups, working agreements and team health checks.

arks.name: developer-environment
arks.description: For teams that want one-command setup: bootstrap scripts, devcontainers or Nix shells, task runners and fast pre-commit hooks.

arks.name: code-quality-gates
arks.description: For teams raising the code quality floor: linter strategy, baselined static analysis, complexity limits and fast merge gates.

arks.name: feature-flags
arks.description: For teams shipping behind flags: flag lifecycle and ownership, progressive rollouts with kill switches, flag cleanup and trunk-based development.

arks.name: error-handling-design
arks.description: For developers designing robust code paths: error types and propagation, helpful error messages, retries with backoff and defensive checks at boundaries.

arks.name: clean-code
arks.description: For developers who want code others can read: intent-revealing names, small functions, simple design, lower cognitive complexity and smell detection.

arks.name: technical-specs
arks.description: For engineers turning product asks into buildable work: technical specs, testable acceptance criteria, edge-case enumeration and spec review.

arks.name: engineering-standards
arks.description: For staff engineers and heads of engineering: a lean style guide, an engineering handbook, a technology radar and architecture principles.

arks.name: agentic-coding
arks.description: For developers working with AI coding agents: project instruction files, precise task briefs, verification loops and reviewing AI-generated diffs.

arks.name: test-writing-agents
arks.description: For teams growing test coverage: agents that write unit, integration and property-based tests and the test data builders they need.

arks.name: e2e-testing-agents
arks.description: For web teams: agents that map critical journeys, generate Playwright tests, triage e2e failures and migrate Cypress suites.

arks.name: tdd-pair-agents
arks.description: For developers who want strict TDD with agents: separate test-first, minimal-implementation and refactor agents that keep each other honest.

arks.name: code-review-agents
arks.description: For teams adding agent reviewers: correctness, readability and test-adequacy reviewers, a PR risk assessor and a summary writer that merges their findings.

arks.name: pull-request-agents
arks.description: For developers shipping PRs: agents that write commit messages and PR descriptions, split big branches and work through review feedback.

arks.name: refactoring-agents
arks.description: For teams cleaning up code: agents that scan for smells, plan safe refactorings, execute them step by step and hunt dead code.

arks.name: legacy-modernisation-agents
arks.description: For teams taking on legacy systems: agents that map the system, write characterization tests, assess modernisation options and plan strangler migrations.

arks.name: architecture-review-agents
arks.description: For architects and tech leads: agents that review architecture against principles, critique design docs, draft ADRs and analyse trade-offs.

arks.name: ddd-modeling-agents
arks.description: For teams applying DDD: agents that propose bounded contexts and context maps, model aggregates and facilitate event storming in text.

arks.name: system-design-agents
arks.description: For engineers designing new systems: agents that draft the design, estimate capacity, analyse failure modes and advise on consistency.

arks.name: debugging-agents
arks.description: For developers fixing bugs: agents that reproduce the bug, investigate root cause, bisect regressions and verify the fix.

arks.name: performance-agents
arks.description: For engineers chasing slowness: agents that analyse profiles, run sound benchmarks, track down regressions and optimise hot paths.

arks.name: dependency-upgrade-agents
arks.description: For teams behind on dependencies: agents that plan batched upgrades, find breaking changes that affect you and carry out the upgrade.

arks.name: docs-agents
arks.description: For teams with thin or stale docs: agents that write and edit pages, overhaul READMEs and audit docs for gaps.

arks.name: api-docs-agents
arks.description: For API teams: agents that fill reference gaps, generate runnable examples and catch drift between docs and implementation.

arks.name: release-agents
arks.description: For release owners: agents that draft release notes, curate the changelog, check release readiness and handle backports.

arks.name: oss-maintainer-agents
arks.description: For open source maintainers: agents that triage issues, give first-pass reviews to contributors and sweep stale issues politely.

arks.name: codebase-onboarding-agents
arks.description: For new joiners and their teams: agents that explore a repo, answer questions about it, draw its architecture and write the onboarding guide.

arks.name: monorepo-agents
arks.description: For monorepo owners: agents that audit internal dependencies, work out the scope of a change and plan repo consolidation.

arks.name: git-agents
arks.description: For developers and repo owners: agents that resolve merge conflicts, tidy branch history before merge and clean up stale branches.

arks.name: tech-debt-agents
arks.description: For tech leads: agents that audit a codebase into a debt register, scan hotspots and turn findings into a funded paydown plan.

arks.name: engineering-manager-agents
arks.description: For engineering managers: agents that prepare 1:1s, propose sprint plans, estimate work and write weekly status updates.

arks.name: engineering-insights-agents
arks.description: For engineering leaders: agents that compute DORA and flow metrics, forecast delivery dates and analyse developer experience surveys.

arks.name: developer-experience-agents
arks.description: For platform and DX teams: agents that fix broken dev setups, audit the inner loop for friction and speed up CI.

arks.name: large-scale-change-agents
arks.description: For teams making codebase-wide changes: agents that write and test codemods and roll changes out across owners.

arks.name: test-quality-agents
arks.description: For teams who distrust their tests: agents that find coverage gaps, kill surviving mutants, review test smells and fix flaky tests.

arks.name: spec-agents
arks.description: For engineers and PM-engineer pairs: agents that turn briefs into specs, write acceptance criteria and review specs for gaps before work starts.

arks.name: qa-agents
arks.description: For QA engineers: agents that write test plans and exploratory charters, select regression tests and turn observations into bug reports.

arks.name: event-driven-agents
arks.description: For teams on event-driven architectures: agents that map event flows, review schema changes and design sagas.

arks.name: agentic-coding-agents
arks.description: For developers using coding agents daily: agents that plan implementations, maintain AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and verify AI-written diffs.
